disclosures.name: TestAppendAllocs
disclosures.reason: Want-zero AllocsPerRun assert: Go's binary.Append writes through pre-sized memory without allocating. The converted reflect walk counts golib-runtime objects per run: 75 at go1.24.13 and 9 at go1.26.10 on windows and linux (identical test body). Boxing field values into `any` is not among them: golib's counter never charges a CLR box (AllocationCounter.cs:50-53), and the value-typed TestSizeAllocs subtests read exactly zero on Windows. The counted sites are not yet attributed; the candidates are on binary.cs's reflect path.
disclosures.history: want-zero AllocsPerRun assert: binary.Append's reflect walk boxes every field value into `any` (Value readers) in the managed model where Go's encoder writes through pre-sized memory allocation-free; boxing into an interface allocates on the CLR by construction. RELABEL 2026-09-23 (C1, as ruled at ledger 2026-09-23 03:37 O2): alloc-profile -> deferred. The boxing proof above is WITHDRAWN and FALSIFIED: the counter never charges a CLR box (AllocationCounter.cs:50-53), and the value-typed TestSizeAllocs subtests read exact zero on Windows (readings-go1.24.13.tsv lines 84-86), which a per-call box could not. RE-READ AT go1.26.10 (2026-10-25, G): reading moved from 75 per run at go1.24.13 to 9 per run on windows and linux; the test body is identical at go1.24.13 and go1.26.10.

disclosures.name: TestSizeAllocs/*binary.Struct
disclosures.reason: Want-zero AllocsPerRun assert on Size of a *Struct: Go's non-escaping interface argument allocates nothing. Boxing the pointer argument is not the cause: golib's counter never charges a CLR box (AllocationCounter.cs:50-53), and the value-typed TestSizeAllocs subtests read exactly zero on Windows. At go1.26.10 golib's counter charges no object on this path and the measurable figure is bytes, 192 per run on windows and linux; the candidate site is binary.cs's Indirect over ValueOf.
